findings.checklist_item: Specify the intra-response ordering rule for a batch containing both a record call and repository evidence call(s): state whether banked_ids() is re-read (and the current id recomputed) before or after the same-response evidence call is counted/executed, and whether a same-response record of the current id suppresses that response's step-3 fallback.
evidence: Plan: 'select one repository evidence action per response ... At most one record_criterion_verdict call executes per response. A record for the current id advances the live bank boundary'

Plan defines current id as 'the first criterion_ids entry absent from the live banked_ids() result' and the counter reset as that 'observable bank transition' — but pydantic-ai runs a response's tool batch concurrently, so a batch mixing a record and an evidence call has no stated ordering between the boundary advance and the evidence-step count

The worked example only covers responses that issue a pure read/search batch (steps 1,2,3) and a separate later record-only revision; it never covers a response carrying both a record and an evidence call
findings.finding: The wrapper decision rule for a single model response that contains BOTH a record_criterion_verdict call and one-or-more repository evidence calls is not co-located/specified: it is unclear whether the record's bank-boundary advance is observed before or after the same-response evidence call is counted against and executed for the current id, which determines which id's counter the evidence step increments and whether a just-recorded id can still receive a step-3 fallback in the same response.
findings.location: Repair design -> Wrapper state, composition, and progress guarantee
scenarios: A dense run where the model, in one response, banks id A via record_criterion_verdict AND issues a read/search batch intended for id B
A step-3 response for id A that simultaneously records A/met=true and issues evidence calls — ambiguous whether the same-response step-3 fallback still fires against A
findings.suggested_fix: Add a co-located rule: within one response, apply the record call's bank upsert (and boundary advance) FIRST under the shared lock, THEN recompute the current id from live banked_ids() before counting/executing that response's governed repository call — so a same-response record of id A moves the counter to the new current id and cannot trigger a fallback over A.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that the first-call-per-run_step detection and its executed-marker write occur atomically under the same shared lock (check-then-mark inside the lock), not just the fallback_record write, so concurrent same-step extras cannot both execute.
evidence: 'the first call at a ctx.run_step executes through the wrapped stack; concurrent extras at that step receive a fixed COMMIT steering notice and do not execute'
'Pydantic AI executes a response tool batch concurrently'
the lock is named explicitly only for fallback_record: 'invokes fallback_record under the shared lock'
findings.finding: The first-call detection/mark for a governed repository call at a given ctx.run_step is a check-then-act that must be atomic to reject concurrent extras, but the plan only explicitly names the shared lock for the fallback_record write, leaving the first-call gate's atomicity under-specified against Pydantic AI's concurrent batch execution.
findings.location: Repair design -> Wrapper state, composition, and progress guarantee
scenarios: Two concurrent read/search calls at the same run_step both pass the 'is this the first call?' check before either marks the step executed, so both execute a real repository tool and the one-execution-per-response invariant breaks.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify that the executed-marker check-and-set for a ctx.run_step is performed under the shared asyncio.Lock, so exactly one coroutine wins the first-call gate and the rest are steered without executing.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that the completion wrapper writes the per-run_step executed-marker synchronously (under the shared lock, before any await into the wrapped tool) so the 'first-call-at-step executes / extras get COMMIT notice' decision is atomic, matching the memo layer's between-awaits guarantee.
evidence: Plan: 'the first call at a ctx.run_step executes through the wrapped stack; concurrent extras at that step receive a fixed COMMIT steering notice and do not execute'

_memo_toolsets docstring pins that dict get/create 'runs to completion between awaits on the single event loop, so two coroutines cannot race'; _runaway_guard_toolsets uses checked_steps membership set BEFORE any await

Unlike the runaway guard (which only appends a signature and computes a ratio synchronously), the completion gate must decide 'first-at-step' AND then hold that decision across the wrapped tool's await, so the per-step executed-marker must be written synchronously before yielding or a concurrent extra could also see itself as first
findings.finding: The load-bearing 'one repository execution per response' gate is a check-then-act (determine first-at-run_step, then await the wrapped tool execution) whose atomicity is only partially specified; the plan should pin exactly which state is written before any await, as the memo layer does.
findings.location: Repair design -> Wrapper state, composition, and progress guarantee
scenarios: A parallel read/search/list batch at one run_step where two coroutines both read the executed-marker as unset before either sets it -> two real repository executions in one response, violating the one-execution invariant the eval pins
findings.suggested_fix: State that on entry the wrapper acquires the shared lock, tests-and-sets the per-run_step executed-marker atomically, and only the coroutine that set it proceeds to await the wrapped tool; all others release the lock and return the COMMIT notice without executing.

evidence: 6 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.finding: The formal '## Acceptance criteria' checklist and the 'Proposed resolution (KERNEL, affirmative-framed)' describe a prompt-only fix (co-locate banking directive into the manifest), but the later 'Phase 2 scope expansion after held-out RED' explicitly states three prompt-only repairs were REJECTED and the delivered mechanism is now a toolset-wrapper interceptor. The top-of-plan ACs and KERNEL proposal are stale relative to the final mechanism, so an executor reading top-down would implement the abandoned approach.
findings.location: ## Acceptance criteria / ## Proposed resolution (KERNEL) vs ## Phase 2 scope expansion after held-out RED
findings.suggested_fix: Replace or annotate the '## Acceptance criteria' block so it enumerates the wrapper deliverable's ACs (0/3 RED current prompt, >=2/3 GREEN repaired, simple control PASS, mutation returns RED, wrapper unit tests) and mark the KERNEL prompt-only proposal as superseded.

findings.finding: The Phase-2 toolset-wrapper mechanism reinvents primitives that already exist as three WrapperToolset layers in the same module (src/rebar/llm/agent_call.py) without citing that prior art or justifying a fourth wrapper.
findings.location: Plan section '## Phase 2 scope expansion after held-out RED' (the pydantic-ai toolset wrapper seam paragraph); updated file impact does not list agent_call.py additions in relation to existing wrappers
findings.suggested_fix: In the Phase-2-expansion section, add a short prior-art paragraph citing the three existing wrappers; either (a) extend `_steering_toolsets` with a per-cycle one-call-per-response bound (it already advertises-but-steers past a boundary and reads ctx.run_step), reusing `_memo_toolsets`'s per-key asyncio.Lock pattern for the parallel-batch serialization, or (b) if a distinct wrapper is truly warranted, name its exact slot in the innermost->outermost order and describe its interaction with the memo cache and runaway signature window.

findings.finding: The 'Caller and compatibility scope' inventory for successor_system_prompt claims it 'feed[s] only CompletionAgentStep and their tests' and the file-impact / focused-suite lists name only tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_banking.py, but tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_prefetch.py:321-322 also references successor_system_prompt and asserts on its output. That referencing test file is omitted from both the file-impact list and the deterministic run command, so the caller sweep is provably incomplete.
findings.location: 'Caller and compatibility scope' and 'Testing and verification' / 'Updated file impact'
findings.suggested_fix: Run find_referencing_symbols on successor_system_prompt, note test_completion_prefetch.py:321 as a referencing site, and either include it in the focused-suite run command or explicitly document that its assertion targets the static prefix (unchanged by the addendum rewrite) and is therefore unaffected.

findings.finding: The Phase 2 wrapper is activated by 'private, non-schema metadata naming a three-step repository-evidence cycle' on the completion record tool, but the metadata's shape (key names, value vocabulary, the count '3', which tools it governs) and its attachment point on the tool object are never defined — and agent_call.py has no metadata-detection concept today.
findings.location: Plan §'Phase 2 scope expansion after held-out RED'

findings.finding: The plan does not specify the fallback when, after the three-call evidence bound steers subsequent repository calls to the record transition, the model STILL emits no record_criterion_verdict for the current id.
findings.location: Plan §'Phase 2 scope expansion' ('After three executed evidence responses it ... steers repository calls to the record transition. One successful record_criterion_verdict call is allowed per response and resets the cycle')

findings.finding: The KERNEL proposal and the Phase 2 repair give an executor contradictory directions for the same manifest artifact: co-locate an imperative per-criterion banking directive INTO the manifest vs. keep the manifest data-only with no imperative text.
findings.location: Plan §'Proposed resolution (KERNEL)' step 1 vs. §'Phase 2 repair plan' ('Keep the criterion manifest inside ticket_context as data only ... with no imperative text')
findings.suggested_fix: Add a one-line note under the KERNEL heading: 'Superseded by Phase 2 — the banking imperative moves to system authority; the manifest becomes data-only (drop completion_banking.py:184-188 imperative lines).'

findings.finding: The title and 'Proven root cause' section assert the epic verifier 'banks zero verdicts' across full and 4x budget, but the later 'Phase 2 scope expansion after held-out RED' reports the pre-fix arm banked ALL FIVE criteria (17 calls, then 11 bank points in 3/3 trials). These two narratives contradict each other on the core observable, so the plan's stated intent ('banks zero') is no longer faithfully proven by its own final evidence, and the RED oracle basis shifts from 'zero banks' to a bounded-trial threshold without reconciling the original headline claim.
findings.location: Title + 'Proven root cause' vs 'Phase 2 scope expansion after held-out RED'
findings.suggested_fix: Retitle/reframe the defect to the confirmed mechanism (parallel/batched tool calls prevent the per-criterion bounded loop under a bounded request budget, so the run either exhausts budget before finalizing or over-consumes evidence calls) and state the exact RED metric (bounded-trial banking behavior) consistently across the summary, root cause, and Phase 2 sections.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that when criterion_ids is empty the completion policy is not attached (or the wrapper is an explicit no-op), preserving the existing fail-open primary behavior and byte-identical kwargs.
evidence: Plan: 'CompletionAgentStep.run attaches the policy to the primary record tool after loading the expected criteria/id map'
completion_recovery.py _primary_manifest returns '' when 'not expected' (empty criteria) and on any read/parse failure
Plan: 'The current id is always the first criterion_ids entry absent from the live banked_ids() result' — undefined when criterion_ids is empty
findings.finding: The plan does not specify wrapper behavior when criterion_ids is empty (e.g. the primary manifest read returns '' or explicit_completion_criteria yields no criteria), where the 'current id = first criterion_ids entry absent from banked_ids()' boundary has no first entry.
findings.location: Repair design -> Completion-only enforcement policy / Wrapper state
scenarios: A ticket whose criteria fail to load produces empty expected criteria; if the policy still attaches with an empty criterion_ids tuple, the current-id boundary and fallback_record have no target id
findings.suggested_fix: State that CompletionAgentStep.run and _run_one_successor skip policy attachment when the resolved id list is empty (mirroring _primary_manifest's fail-open ''), so no attribute is set and existing tool behavior is byte-identical.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Capture the completion-wrapper layer rationale and the `_rebar_completion_evidence_policy` composition-order invariant in a durable doc (module docstring / AGENTS.md / ADR), and cover it with an acceptance criterion.
evidence: 'A distinct completion wrapper is required because global steering is keyed only to an absolute run step; completion needs a live per-criterion boundary...'
'A new substantive module owns the policy and wrapper'
no acceptance criterion or step names an ADR/AGENTS.md/design-doc update for the new layer/metadata contract
findings.finding: The plan introduces a novel toolset-layer pattern (a completion evidence policy wrapper distinct from steering/memo/runaway layers) and a private `_rebar_completion_evidence_policy` metadata contract, but names no durable design-doc/ADR/AGENTS.md update capturing why this fourth layer and metadata seam exist.
findings.location: Repair design -> Completion-only enforcement policy / Wrapper state
scenarios: A future maintainer adds a fifth toolset layer or changes composition order without knowing why completion sits inside runaway but outside memo, and reintroduces the exhaustion bug.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC requiring the new module's docstring (or an AGENTS.md/ADR entry) to document the innermost->outermost composition order and the fail-closed metadata contract.
